endpoint.text: The primary objective was to compare tirzepatide with placebo in HbA1c change from baseline at 12 weeks.
Secondary efficacy objectives were to compare each dose-escalation regimen of tirzepatide with placebo for change in mean body weight, fasting blood glucose (FBG) and waist circumference.

reported_results.text: At week 12, absolute HbA1c change from baseline (SE) was greater in the tirzepatide treatment groups compared with placebo (placebo, +0.2% [0.21]; 12 mg, −1.7% [0.19]; 15 mg-1, −2.0% [0.20]; 15 mg-2, −1.8% [0.19]).
The mean age was 57.4 years, HbA1c 8.4% and body mass index 31.9 kg/m2 .

The average age, HbA1c, BMI and duration of diagnosed type 2 diabetes were 57.4 years, 8.4% (67.8 mmol/mol), 31.9 kg/m2 and 9.1 years, respectively; 59.5% of patients were male and 86.5% of patients were on metformin. 3.2 | Efficacy After 12 weeks of treatment, HbA1c significantly decreased from baseline in the three tirzepatide treatment groups compared with placebo (Figure 2A).

The number of patients with the combined AEs of nausea, vomiting and/or diarrhoea was numerically greater in the tirzepatide 15 mg-1 treatment group (57.1%) compared with the 12 mg group (48.3%) and the 15 mg-2 group (46.4%); all of the tirzepatide treatment groups reported more nausea, vomiting and/or diarrhoea than placebo (11.5%).
